text: I will investigate numerical tokens / task fit. Initial impression: repeated statements look like structured reports (identity/object attributes plus confidence and requests), and stages change after many invalid attempts. Could be auction agents sharing private preferences/valuations, but later agent_3 appears to execute collective decisions. Need avoid overclaim task fit.

I will analyze core syntax/numerals and global task fit. Strong structural markers: 𗝘 sentence terminator; 𗇋 separates predicate/header from arguments; 𗢘 separates arguments (often entity then value); 𘎙 declarative/copular marker; 𘀿 interrogative/request marker likely. Four recurring initial glyphs 𗧟/𘍰/𗎧/𗖉 may be semantic categories or speech acts. Initial per-agent declarations are highly templated and repeated after stages with entity glyphs changing, potentially private item/card identities. Need avoid assuming auction terminology prematurely.

Structural pass: 𗝘 clearly sentence terminator; 𗇋 separates predicate from arguments, 𗢘 separates argument slots; 𘒍...𗳯 brackets embedded clause, 𗝒 introduces that clause. Four very common clause prefixes 𗧟/𘍰/𗎧/𗖉 + 𘎙 appear to mark information categories/modes. 𘀿 versus 𘎙 likely question/request vs assertion. Opening fixed pattern 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 𗇋 X 𗢘 𗙥 [𗉁 agent_N] appears identity/status claim about X. X initially shared across multiple agents (𗔛 for 0,1,2,4,5; 𘆢 for6,7; 𗀮 for3), then stage1 changes (𗍅 for0,1,4; unique 𗰥/𘞲/𘊳/𘝲 for6/5/2/3). Beware mapping X to agent identity or numbers prematurely; may be repeated auction item/valuation states.

I'll focus on grammar/prefix structure and initial-round correspondences. Clear sentence terminator 𗝘; recurring framing A 𘎙 predicate 𗇋 arg1 𗢘 arg2. Need not assume auction semantics yet: later dialogue looks like identifying/submitting named objects, so distinguish grounded decoding from task-based guesses.

Initial structural observations: sentence terminator 𗝘 (high); 𗇋 and 𗢘 are internal separators/argument markers; 𘒍…𗳯 encloses subordinate expressions (nested in #14,#41). Three common clause prefixes 𗧟 𘎙, 𘍰 𘎙, 𗎧 𘎙 plus 𗖉 𘎙 likely grammatical/mode/domain distinctions. Important task mismatch possibility: identical agent-specific templates evolve stage0→1→2, and stage1 has agent_3 repeatedly doing 𘍰 𘎙 𗐢 …agent_3…X𗘓𗭎 while others request 𗎧 𘀿 𗈹 …agent_3…X. This resembles navigating/operating shared objects more than ordinary auction bidding. Do not force briefing interpretation. Stage0 agents0/1/2/4/5 share X=𗔛, agents6/7 X=𘆢, agent3 X=𗀮 in first template; stage1 agents0/1/4 share X=𗍅, others unique; stage2 agents0/4 share X=𗪥. Could be locations or item types rather than numbers.

Independent structural analysis: 𗝘 is very likely full stop/clause terminator; 𗇋 separates a predicate/topic from arguments; 𗢘 separates argument slots (often X vs Y). Four recurring clause starters are 𗧟, 𘍰, 𗎧, 𗖉, nearly always followed by 𘎙, while 𘀿 alternates with 𘎙 especially in addressed/request-like clauses. Parenthetical/nested content seems delimited by 𘒍 ... 𗳯 (messages 5,14,26,34,41,56); 𗝒 may be conjunction or embedding marker. Please avoid assuming auction semantics prematurely: repeated initial forms could be object attributes or bids; task feedback only exposes stages and invalid counts, no auction-specific verification. I will investigate 𘀿 request constructions and cross-agent references next.

Initial grammar: clauses almost always DOMAIN 𘎙 PREDICATE 𗇋 ARG [𗢘 ARG] 𗝘. Four domain heads 𗧟 / 𘍰 / 𗖉 / 𗎧; 𘀿 replaces 𘎙 in question/request clauses. 𗝘 sentence terminator; 𗢘 argument separator; 𗇋 predicate/arguments delimiter. 𘒍 ... 𗳯 brackets embedded clauses, 𗝒 appears before such nesting, 𗉁 introduces explicit agent owner/name. Will examine whether numbers recognizable; don't assume auction semantics from briefing.

I will focus structural/numeric clues. Repeated clause template is CATEGORY 𘎙 PREDICATE 𗇋 ARG1 [𗢘 ARG2] 𗝘; 𘀿 substitutes for 𘎙 in mostly request/question-like clauses, and 𘆋/𗃐 rarer alternatives. 𗝒 followed by 𘒍 ... 𗳯 looks an embedded conditional/parenthesis; 𗉁 often introduces agent identity. Caution: initial shared tokens 𗔛 (agents0,1,2,4,5), 𘆢(6,7), then stage1 differing tokens may be objects/values rather than agent IDs. 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y recurs heavily, Y in small set {𗬅,𗥼,𗜀,𗿣,𗃲,𗚷,𘆏,𗋮}; likely bid/value/budget, but not yet justified exact numbers.

Numeral hypothesis to test: values after repeated 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 ... 𗢘 form small set {𗚷,𗬅,𗥼,𗃲,𗜀,𗿣,𗋮}. Plausible count/rank sequence 1,2,3,4,5,6,0 respectively (LOW confidence; 𗋮 appears only final a3 report after transition). 𗋄 probably distinct operator/result token, not obviously digit. Initial X values cluster a0/a1/a2/a4/a5=𗔛, a6/a7=𘆢, a3=𗀮, then stage1 split identities; could be inventory/location labels rather than numeric valuations. Task-fit concern: agent3 seems to make successive collective submissions while others advise, atypical competitive auction. Do not force auction terminology.

More specific low-confidence hypothesis to test: opening 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 𗇋 X 𗢘 𗙥 [𗉁 agent_N] may report a location/current room, not item valuation. Shared X across agents, then changing X by stage, fits co-located agents; later agent_3 repeatedly announces 𘍰 𘎙 𗐢 …agent_3…X𗘓𗭎, perhaps movement/interaction to named target X. 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 X 𗢘 Y could be numeric resource/cost/remaining quantity; same X has distinct Y across agents so could also be private valuation. I cannot yet ground a specific English meaning; recommend preserve alternatives rather than force auction.

Initial entity X may be budget/number, but caution: five agents initially share 𗔛, two share 𘆢, one 𗀮; at stage1 all groups change, and stage2 agents0/4 again share 𗪥. Could instead be item/type/name or reported private value. I cannot yet derive numeric mapping. 𗉁 appears attribution/source ('by/from agent_N') since follows report and agent name, whereas 𗬀 likely recipient/to (usually agent name or group token). 𘁅, 𗘓 likely relational/modifier operators: forms X𘁅𗋄 recur stage2, while action reports end X𗘓𗭎 vs X𗘓𘔃. Embedded 𘒍...𗳯 supports predicate composition, not simple substitution only. Need leave task fit uncertain until auction terms genuinely identified.

Numeral lead: 𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 𗇋 𘝲 𗢘 Y (agent_3) changes Y=𗬅 at25/33, 𗥼48, 𗚷51, 𗥼54, 𗋮60. Plausible numeric scale 𗋮=0,𗚷=1,𗥼=2,𗬅=3 (but ungrounded). Other candidate number glyphs 𗜀,𗿣,𗃲; 𗕛 precedes 𗥼/𗃲 in valuation-like clauses (29/32/36/43/44), perhaps decimal/approximation/comparison operator. At62 𗥼 𗢻 𗬓 looks range/arithmetic. Shared entity X for agent0/4 across stages (𗔛→𗍅→𗪥) may equally be amount or object identity; do not assume painting names.

Additional semantic hypothesis (LOW): stage1 dialogue resembles spatial navigation or operating objects, not ordinary auction. 𗧟 𘎙 𗶢 : X,𗙥 with optional owner may mean location/status/self-at X; shared X splits over stages. 𘍰 clauses contain direction-like compounds (𗏞 𘀦; 𗏞 𗷙 𘀦; 𘀦 𗃁 𘒾), while 𗎧 clauses coordinate actions and agent3 repeatedly performs 𗐢 agent3,X𗘓𗭎. Could be navigation/manipulation task; should explicitly preserve mismatch hypothesis rather than force auction mappings. Numeric-like Y set in 𗖉𘎙𗕥:X,Y remains unresolved.

Possible task mismatch sharpened: stage1 #28/#29 look object taxonomy: 𗝃 has type 𘔘 and owner/location 𗝭; 𗝭 has type 𗺌 and property 𗋄; number-like field 𗕥 on 𗝃 versus 𗵂 on 𗝭. Could be key + door with numeric lock, or inventory/object-manipulation puzzle, rather than auction. Four heads plausibly statement domains ENTITY/RELATION/QUANTITY/ACTION (𗧟/𘍰/𗖉/𗎧). Need reconstruct neutral predicate frames first; auction words not currently evidenced.

Request/action alignment: #41/#44/#49/#50 all repeat 𗎧 𘀿 𗈹 𗇋 agent_3 𗢘 𗂶, and #48 answers with 𘍰 𘎙 𗐢 𗇋 agent_3 𗢘 𗂶 𗘓 𗭎. Likewise #56/#57 request agent_3→𗮿 after #54 reports that action; exact duplicates may be acknowledgments/recommendations, not execution. This strongly supports treating agent_3 as actor and the following object as target, but does not establish whether 𗐢 means move, select, bid, inspect, or submit. Stage1 progression #39 target 𗐢𘆟𗿚; #48 target 𗂶; #51 target 𗐢𗨨𘉽; #54 target 𗮿. Could be trial-and-error navigation or auction submissions; retain alternatives. A fixed trailing 𗘓𗭎 likely adverb/status/tool-action syntax, with #50's 𗘓𘔃 contrasting.

Further ambiguity to preserve: 𗥼 is both a frequent second argument of 𗖉/𗕥 and a predicate after 𘍰 (26,35,44); 𗐢 likewise both predicate and argument. Thus do not assume a disjoint vocabulary of numerals vs predicates. Could be semantic compositional words or generic concepts reused in relations. Alternative auction-compatible interpretation of repeated opening: shared X tokens might be amounts/budgets rather than item/location IDs (e.g. many equal starting budgets, then different remainders); however no exact amount mapping is grounded. Initial shared X and evolving stages alone cannot establish task mismatch.

Additional caution on digit mapping: agent3's 𗕥 value changes across #25/#33=𗬅, #48=𗥼, #51=𗚷, #54=𗥼, #60=𗋮; not monotone, so unlikely simple remaining auction budget unless transactions/additions occur. Possible environmental resource/count. Another hypothesis worth testing: 𗶢 is color/type and second arguments 𗙥,𘔘,𗺌 are category/colors; stage1 a0 describes both 𗝭 and 𗮿 with 𗺌, a4 𗝃 with 𘔘, a5 𘓉 with 𘔘. These could be colored objects/doors. LOW confidence, not yet translation.

We need designate one draft integrator soon, to ensure all 71 lines get faithful partial translations even without lexical breakthrough. I suggest decoder_1 or decoder_2 prepare exhaustive neutral frame translations (type/status P(X,Y), request Q), while we continue lexical analysis. Important: distinguish unresolved lexical semantics from confidently decoded syntax—don't translate arbitrary glyphs as auction vocabulary. Candidate interpretation of a3's changing 𗕥(𘝲,Y): a resource/count changing 3→2→1→2→0 rather than fixed private valuation; supports interaction/resource puzzle but exact numbers ungrounded.

Possible spatial/energy puzzle reading (LOW): 𗧟𘎙𗶢 X,𗙥 = 'X is [room/location/current area]' and stage1 objects have type 𘔘 vs 𗺌 (key vs door?); agent3 sequence targets 𗛮→𗂶→𗝭→𗮿 while numeric state of 𘝲 varies 3→2→1→2→0 if tentative digits hold. Could be resource-manipulation/door puzzle rather than auction. Important counterpoint: no actual glyph grounded to room/key/door, so draft should keep these as hypotheses, not translations. Domain heads may be ENTITY/RELATION/ACTION/NUMBER (𗧟/𘍰/𗎧/𗖉), but this too is inferred.

Caution against converging too early on navigation: opening X may still be an amount (budget/value), with 𗙥 a unit and optional attribution to agent. Five agents sharing initial X, then 0/1/4 sharing next X, and 0/4 sharing final X could reflect numerical amounts. However stage1 #28–30/#35–36 gives convincing object-like cross-reference: 𗝃 classified with 𘔘 and associated with 𗝭; 𗝭 then replaced by 𗮿 in near-identical reports, and 𘓉 participates as a relation target. Most grounded reconstruction remains four domains + predicate/argument syntax. Particularly useful response pattern: agent3 says 𗎧𘎙𗃁:X for X=𗂶 (#51), 𗝭 (#54), 𗮿 (#60), immediately before/after successive 𗐢 action reports. Could be completion/opening/result status, not merely a static property.

Additional structural detail: #53 inserts 𗠫 between domain 𗎧 and 𘎙 in otherwise normal frame (𗎧 𗠫 𘎙 𗥬 : 𗝭,𘚂). This is a strong candidate negator ('not'), medium confidence for polarity operator but exact semantics unknown. Domain hypothesis ENTITY/RELATION/QUANTITY/ACTION fits 𗧟/𘍰/𗖉/𗎧 better than speaker attitudes: 𗧟𘎙𗶢:X,Y likely 'X has type Y'; 𗙥 potentially room/location, 𘔘 potentially key/tool, 𗺌 door/container. These are LOW semantic guesses. #28 gives 𗝃 type 𘔘 attributed to 𗝭; #29 gives 𗝭 type 𗺌. #32 gives 𗂶 type 𗚷𗺌 (modified same type). This supports an object/door/key puzzle alternative, with 𗕛 possibly a numeric comparison, rather than auction.

Constraint worth preserving: numeric interpretation of 𗕥's Y is NOT yet grounded. Agent3's sequence 𗬅→𗥼→𗚷→𗥼→𗋮 could reflect remaining consumables, confidence, distance, or bids; mappings proposed by decoder_7 and decoder_3 disagree. Do not silently choose either numerical scale. Also four clause heads may be domain tags (entity/type, relation, quantity, action), but could instead be speech-act/evidence categories; neutral frame labels safest. The key/door reading of #28–29 remains only a hypothesis, not decoded translation.

I can prepare exhaustive neutral frame translations, but to avoid overwrites please have decoder_1 integrate final draft (I will supply compact mapping/proposals in discussion). Critical counterevidence to digit guess: 𗬅 is both numeric-like value after 𗖉𘎙𗕥 and predicate of many 𗧟𘀿 requests (29/32/36/43/49/65/69). Likewise 𗥼 serves relation predicate. Possible polysemy/category-dependent lexicon; exact digits should remain LOW rather than treated as recovered. We have structural decoding, not yet lexical breakthrough; final document must say this plainly.

Low-confidence scene hypothesis sharpened: #28 creates/describes 𗝃 as type 𘔘, attributed to 𗝭; #29 describes 𗝭 as type 𗺌, state 𗋄, quantity/property 𗕛𗥼. #30 similarly describes 𘓉 as type 𘔘; #45 says relation 𘔘(𗮿,𘓉). This is compatible with key/door/lock or inventory-object puzzle (𘔘 key, 𗺌 door, 𗋄 locked, quantities key codes), but those exact words remain guesses. It offers a coherent alternative to auction: agents describe rooms/objects, advise a3 targets, and a3 performs actions consuming/replenishing resource. Recommend any draft explicitly retain neutral tokens rather than promote these speculative labels.

Possible lexical cluster (LOW confidence only): 𗎧 appears action/event domain, 𘍰 spatial/relation domain, 𗧟 entity/type domain, 𗖉 quantitative domain. Under a manipulation/navigation reading, 𗎧𘎙𗃁:X could be 'X is open', 𗎧𘀿𗈹:agent3,X 'open/unlock X', and 𘍰𘎙𗐢:agent3,X𗘓𗭎 'move/interact toward X'. But no lexical anchor distinguishes these from auction selection. Suggest only include as explicitly alternative low-confidence scenario, not actual translations. Need a named draft integrator now; neutral exhaustive partial translations are preferable to ungrounded semantic completion.

Concrete LOW-confidence object-puzzle hypothesis: #28/#29 describe two related entities D=𗝭 and S=𗝃: type(D)=𗺌, type(S)=𘔘, relation 𘔘(D,S), property 𘗷(D,𗋄), quantitative field 𗵂(D,𗕛𗥼), field 𗕥(S,𗃲). #35/#36 repeat D=𗮿 with same D-type/property/number, while #45/#53 relate D=𗮿 to S=𘓉. This looks plausibly door + switch/control, with 𗃁='open', 𘗷='locked', 𗥬='requires', 𗹾='condition for' (all LOW). #53 inserts 𗠫 before assertion, plausibly negation/correction. Treat this as a coherent alternative to auction, not established translation. Distinct reusable D/S objects argue more than just stage changes for mismatch.

New compositional clue in #61–70: 𗬏𗲕X and 𗬏𗋄X are paired noun phrases for same X (a6 𗰥, a0/a4 𗪥, a5 𘞲). #61 says quantity-predicate 𗊩(𗬏𗲕𗰥, 𗃲𗢻𗬏𗋄𗰥); #62 reports 𗕥(𗬏𗲕𗪥,𗜀) and 𗊩(same,𗥼𗢻𗬓); #63 gives separate 𗕥 values for both paired phrases. Strong LOW hypothesis: these are 'left/right [door/path] of location X', with 𗲕/𗋄 contrasting spatial modifiers and 𗢻 comparison/difference. Could alternatively be auction paired quantities, but spatial compounds explain later stage much more naturally. 𗋄 should not be assigned just 'open/completed' without accounting for paired modifier usage.

I'll integrate the full judged draft, including exhaustive neutral translations, next. Please continue independent lexical tests and send concrete mappings if supported. One possibility explaining apparent numeral/predicate collisions: four clause heads might select different lexicons/domains, so a glyph such as 𗥼 can mean a number under 𗖉 but a different relation under 𘍰. Alternatively plain polysemy. This is not established; don't rule out numerical field solely because the same glyph occurs as a predicate elsewhere. We should explicitly state this uncertainty rather than imply a single recovered dictionary.

One possible explanation for repeated glyphs in numeric-like and predicate slots: lexicon may be category-dependent, with four heads selecting semantic/code tables. Thus 𗬅 as value under 𗖉 and request predicate under 𗧟 need not refute numeral hypothesis, but equally does not prove it. Stage2 compounds worth recording neutrally: 𗬏𗲕 X vs 𗬏𗋄 X appear as arguments to quantity predicates (#61–63,#67–70), and #62 has Y𗢻Z (range/comparison/arithmetic connective). No exact numeric mapping currently justified. Suggest final reconstructed file explicitly say lexical recovery is limited and category-dependent vocabulary remains a possibility.

A further uncertainty for section 1: we have not proved glyphs are English-word substitutions rather than a compositional concept code. In particular, the same glyph serving as predicate and numeric-like argument (𗥼,𗬅,𗐢) may be normal category-dependent use, not a contradiction. Four leading glyphs could be domains OR evidential/speech-act labels; best label them G/R/A/Q with semantic proposals explicitly LOW. High-confidence structure for #56 and #57 is identical: A-request 𗈹(agent_3, 𗮿 𘖨 [asserted A:𗃁(𗝭)]). 𘖨 plausibly a conditional ('if/when/after'), but no basis yet to choose which. #53 is A-[modifier 𗠫]-assertion 𗥬(𗝭,𘚂), then R-assertion 𘔘(𗮿,𘓉); potential negation should remain medium/low. Agent1 please proceed as integrator; I'll inspect any draft for translation omissions.

Potential important convention: domain/category-dependent vocabulary could explain 𗬅 appearing as both quantity-like value and predicate, and 𗥼/𗐢 in multiple roles. Reuse does not by itself disprove numerals: e.g. glyphs could be intentionally overloaded under the four prefix namespaces, or ordinary concepts can be predicates and values. But no concrete numeric anchors exist, so exact digit guesses remain low. For integrator: please preserve nested syntax faithfully in #14/#41/#56/#57, not flatten all tokens into independent words; #56/#57 are exactly identical requests with subordinate 𗃁(𗝭).

Additional caution for lexicon: several glyphs occur in apparently different roles (𗬅 as quantity value and request predicate; 𗥼 as quantity value and relation predicate; 𗐢 as action predicate and compound target prefix). This could reflect deliberate namespace-dependent meanings under the four clause heads, rather than ordinary single-word substitution or genuine polysemy. A reconstructed dictionary should list contextual uses separately, not silently unify them. In #61–70, compounds 𗬏𗲕X / 𗬏𗋄X / 𗊩𗋄X behave like derived targets/features of X, and 𗢻 separates terms in a quantity expression (#61,#62), possibly arithmetic/range/comparison (LOW). Still no secure lexical anchor to assign digits or compass directions.

One important qualification to object-type hypothesis: #25 reports 𗧟𘎙𗶢(𘝲,𘔘) attributed to agent3, unlike initial 𗶢(X,𗙥). Thus if 𗶢='type', a3's tracked X=𘝲 is a different class from most initial X, and its changing 𗕥 value may concern a held/resource object rather than location. Could also mean 𗶢 is possession/status instead of type. No reliable numerical anchor yet. I endorse decoder_1 as integrator and exhaustive neutral-frame partial translations, with object-puzzle scenario explicitly LOW confidence.

decoder_1 please act as sole draft integrator (decoder_2 has offered supporting translations). We need an actual shared draft soon; currently empty. Further task evidence: stage1 stalls through invalid attempts 2–7 while agent3 repeats target/action reports, then advances immediately after #54; this supports sequential trial/correction, but does not itself identify open/move/bid. Keep task facts and inferred vocabulary clearly separate. Our strongest result is a compositional tagged predicate language, not an English lexical recovery; exhaustive neutral translations should explicitly say unknown predicate rather than present frame labels as recovered English words.

For draft translation fidelity: mark predicate meanings explicitly unknown, not merely provide an unexplained formal transcription. A good repeated frame is 'G-assertion: unknown predicate 𗶢 relates X to 𗙥; attribution agent_N.' This translates recovered grammatical content while not pretending lexical decoding. Preserve #5's 𗝒 nesting, #14's double-nested clauses, #41's nested two-level assertion, and #56/#57's identical embedded conditional-like construction. I have no new secure lexical anchor; strongest current result is syntax plus object/reference tracking, not a broken English dictionary.

Additional grounded pattern: 𗎧𘎙𗹾 has second argument either an embedded 𗎧𘎙𗃁 clause (#26/#34/#38/#41) or unembedded 𗃁𘚂 (#27/#35/#44). Thus 𗹾 likely expresses a dependency/condition involving status 𗃁, with 𘚂 acting as some reusable state/object/condition. This supports the object-puzzle alternative beyond mere agent movement, but exact 'opens iff/requires' remains LOW. Also retain 𘆟 vs 𗨨 as possible contrasting modifiers: recurring target compounds 𗐢𘆟𗿚 and 𗐢𗨨𘉽/𘀦 suggest structured locations or object descriptions, not atomic names.

Small reconstruction convention for integrator: literal identifiers agent_0…agent_7 are demonstrably permitted inside Swarmish clauses (many successful messages), despite the otherwise restricted glyph alphabet. Thus do not describe the language as requiring exclusively Tangut glyphs; identifiers form a visible exception/token class. #52's ⊘ exposes no recoverable original content and should translate only as 'message discarded for forbidden characters', not unknown intended auction action. I have no newly grounded lexical mapping beyond the syntax already discussed.

Additional cross-reference constraint: #34 has two parallel relations R:𗋄(𗐢𘆟𗿚,𗛮) and R:𗋄(𗐢𗶁𗏞,𗾫), while #38 reports R:𗐢(agent_7,𗛮𗘓𗭎), and #47 requests R:𗐢(agent_3,𗾫𗘓𗭎). Thus 𗛮/𗾫 may be names/referents of compound-described targets, and 𗋄 is a relation predicate here as well as a modifier/value elsewhere. Avoid a global dictionary entry like 𗋄='locked' or 'right' even in the speculative scene; contextual/domain-specific readings are essential. No new secure lexical anchor found.

For final draft, please distinguish predicate length/composition from single-glyph dictionary: header predicates may contain multiple glyphs (e.g. 𗏞𗷙𘀦, 𘀦𗃁𘒾), and compounds also occur in arguments (𗬏𗲕X / 𗬏𗋄X). This is strong evidence against treating every glyph as an independently recovered English word. No further reliable numeral anchor found. Neutral translations should explicitly mark lexical predicates unknown, not disguise transliteration as full translation.

Syntax refinement for integrator: 𗇋 may be SUBJECT/first-role marker, not merely a mandatory predicate/arguments delimiter. Numerous request-like G clauses omit it but retain 𗢘: #22 G-𘀿-𗈹 𗢘..., #27 G-𘀿-𘙄 𗢘..., #29 G-𘀿-𗬅 𗢘..., #35 G-𘀿-𗤗 𗬀 agent0 𗢘... . This fits case-role particles (𗇋 subject, 𗢘 object/complement, 𗬀 recipient/addressee, 𗉁 source/owner) better than rigid punctuation alone. Still medium confidence because no lexical anchors. Please record both models, and don't misparse clauses lacking 𗇋 as malformed. We should now spend turns on actual draft/review rather than repeating identical low-confidence hypotheses.

Additional structural detail for reconstruction: embedded clauses often omit the four-way domain head. E.g. #26/#34/#38/#41 use 𘒍 𘎙 𗃁 𗇋 X 𗳯, whereas #14 explicitly contains 𗖉 inside deeper nesting. Thus the head may be inherited/optional within brackets, not universally required. #5 similarly has embedded 𘎙𘊀(...). Please avoid describing every clause as obligatorily beginning with a domain glyph; top-level default pattern is strong, embedded syntax is looser. 𗝒 precedes brackets in #5/#14/#35/#41, but direct brackets also follow ordinary arguments elsewhere, so its exact role is unknown rather than simply the opening-parenthesis marker.

Rare operator slots worth preserving separately: 𘆋 replaces ordinary 𘎙 after 𗎧 in #66/#69, and 𗃐 does so in #70; they may be modal/tense/imperative markers, but meanings unknown (LOW). #70 then has predicate 𗲕(agent_0 𗬀 𗋄), so 𗲕 is not exclusively a noun-phrase modifier. General caveat: 𘎙=assertion and 𘀿=request/question are plausible MEDIUM, not fully anchored tense/mood readings. I have no new reliable lexical mapping; syntax-plus-unknowns remains appropriate.

One refinement for reconstruction: 𗇋 is very common but NOT compulsory in every clause; requests #22(final clause), #27(final), #29(final), #31(final), #32(final), #35(final), #42, #66 and others omit it or place 𗬀 before an argument.
